messages.content:
You are checking a research plan against a list of experimental controls. You are not asked whether the plan is good. For each control of the list you give two separate answers: CONTENT (does the plan state this control?) and PLACE (is the passage written under an experiment that it can check?).

PLAN. A sequence of actions written one after the other by a planner. Each action adds or revises one proposed experiment and usually has the fields ACTION, TITLE, PROPOSAL, CONTROLS, COST and PREDICTION. Actions are separated by blank lines and are given in the order they were written. Every action counts, including an action that revises an earlier one and an action that looks incomplete.

REFERENCE CONTROLS. A list of experimental controls. Each has an identifier and a description.

CONTENT. Give exactly one content status for each reference control. Judge the content only, wherever the passage is written in the plan.
- "conforme": a passage of the plan states what the description requires (what is compared, held fixed, varied, repeated, measured or excluded). Different wording is fine. Nothing essential is missing or weakened.
- "altere": a passage of the plan states a recognisable but partial, vaguer, reduced or modified version of the control.
- "absent": no passage of the plan states this control.
If the control is stated in several places, keep the best content status found (conforme, then altere, then absent) and quote the passage that earns it. If several passages earn the same best status, quote one whose PLACE is "checks" if there is one.

PLACE. Only for "conforme" and "altere". Read the action that contains your quote, and judge it against the experiment that this action proposes (its TITLE and PROPOSAL), not against the description of the reference control. If that action has no TITLE and no PROPOSAL, answer "general" if the quoted control is general, otherwise "cannot_check".
- "checks": this experiment is one whose result the quoted control would check.
- "cannot_check": this experiment has nothing for the quoted control to compare, hold fixed, vary, repeat, measure or exclude.
- "general": the quoted control names no model, dataset, metric, quantity, condition or comparison that belongs to one experiment; it would apply to any experiment of the plan.
For "absent", PLACE is null. Your PLACE answer must never change your CONTENT answer.

Rules.
1. Judge each reference control on its own. One passage may support several controls.
2. Judge only what is written. Do not credit a control because it would be sensible, usual or implied. Do not lower a status for style, length, order or cost.
3. Evidence. For "conforme" and "altere", quote the passage that carries the control. Copy it character for character from a single action: no ellipsis, no added or removed word, no corrected spelling, no changed punctuation, no paraphrase. Take the shortest passage that is enough: at least 24 characters, at most 300 characters; if the whole field that carries the control is shorter than 24 characters, quote the whole field. A program searches the plan for your quote, word for word; a quote that is not found counts as "absent".
4. For "absent", the quote is null.
5. Give an answer for every reference control, and for no other identifier.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else, in this form:
{"<identifier>": {"content": "conforme" | "altere" | "absent", "quote": "<quote>" | null, "place": "checks" | "cannot_check" | "general" | null}, ...}

PLAN
<<<
ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of removing the warm-up phase on false-alarm rate at fixed recall for Sundrow-M
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Sundrow-M on the Osric code suite and measure false-alarm rate at fixed recall before and after removing the warm-up phase. The comparison between Sundrow-M and Ilexa-6 uses the same decoding settings and the same evaluation script. The analysis is restricted to the examples of the Osric code suite that Sundrow-M answers correctly before the intervention. All runs share one data order for the Osric code suite, so that differences in false-alarm rate at fixed recall cannot come from batching. We expect the effect of removing the warm-up phase to be smaller for Ilexa-6 than for Sundrow-M, because Ilexa-6 was never exposed to the Lowick tabular benchmark. We plan one pilot run on a tenth of the Osric code suite to check that false-alarm rate at fixed recall is not saturated before the full experiment. We also evaluate transfer to the Lowick tabular benchmark without further tuning of Sundrow-M.
CONTROLS: (1) Evaluate on the Lowick tabular benchmark as a held-out distribution. (2) Shuffle the labels of the Osric code suite as a negative control for false-alarm rate at fixed recall. (3) Report edit distance to the reference on the Osric code suite to check that the gain is not an artifact of one metric. (4) Run Sundrow-M on the Osric code suite with five random seeds and report the spread of false-alarm rate at fixed recall. (5) Ablate removing the warm-up phase alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on false-alarm rate at fixed recall.
COST: 32 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in false-alarm rate at fixed recall beyond seed noise on the Osric code suite.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of swapping the tokenizer vocabulary on rank correlation with the gold ordering for Varnok-2B
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Varnok-2B on the Kettering proofs and measure rank correlation with the gold ordering before and after swapping the tokenizer vocabulary. We also evaluate transfer to the Brenna-QA set without further tuning of Varnok-2B. The comparison between Varnok-2B and Brindle-XL uses the same decoding settings and the same evaluation script. All runs share one data order for the Kettering proofs, so that differences in rank correlation with the gold ordering cannot come from batching. Each configuration of Varnok-2B is trained for the same number of steps and evaluated at three checkpoints. We report rank correlation with the gold ordering separately for short and long inputs of the Kettering proofs, since swapping the tokenizer vocabulary may act differently on each. A null result on rank correlation with the gold ordering would still be informative if refusal rate on the Brenna-QA set also stays within its usual range.
CONTROLS: (1) Report refusal rate on the Kettering proofs to check that the gain is not an artifact of one metric. (2) Include Brindle-XL as a baseline under the same training budget. (3) Match the number of training steps between Varnok-2B and Brindle-XL. (4) Ablate swapping the tokenizer vocabulary alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on rank correlation with the gold ordering. (5) Shuffle the labels of the Kettering proofs as a negative control for rank correlation with the gold ordering.
COST: 11 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Rank correlation with the gold ordering degrades on the Brenna-QA set while it holds on the Kettering proofs.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of shuffling the few-shot examples on calibration error for Ostrava-7
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Ostrava-7 on the Halvard corpus and measure calibration error before and after shuffling the few-shot examples. We report calibration error separately for short and long inputs of the Halvard corpus, since shuffling the few-shot examples may act differently on each. A null result on calibration error would still be informative if area under the detection curve on the Tolwyn dialogue logs also stays within its usual range. If calibration error moves while area under the detection curve stays flat, we attribute the change to shuffling the few-shot examples rather than to capacity. We compare against Tessel-9, trained with the same budget on the Halvard corpus. The comparison between Ostrava-7 and Tessel-9 uses the same decoding settings and the same evaluation script. We expect the effect of shuffling the few-shot examples to be smaller for Tessel-9 than for Ostrava-7, because Tessel-9 was never exposed to the Tolwyn dialogue logs. Each configuration of Ostrava-7 is trained for the same number of steps and evaluated at three checkpoints.
CONTROLS: (1) Ablate shuffling the few-shot examples alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on calibration error. (2) Match the number of training steps between Ostrava-7 and Tessel-9. (3) Include Tessel-9 as a baseline under the same training budget. (4) Repeat the evaluation of calibration error on the Halvard corpus with a second prompt template. (5) Shuffle the labels of the Halvard corpus as a negative control for calibration error.
COST: 8 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Calibration error improves by a small but reliable margin on the Halvard corpus.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of freezing the first twelve layers on agreement with the reference labels for Corvane-12
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Corvane-12 on the Senna safety prompts and measure agreement with the reference labels before and after freezing the first twelve layers. All runs share one data order for the Senna safety prompts, so that differences in agreement with the reference labels cannot come from batching. We compare against Dromond-8, trained with the same budget on the Senna safety prompts. We also evaluate transfer to the Marisol summaries without further tuning of Corvane-12. If agreement with the reference labels moves while mean token overlap stays flat, we attribute the change to freezing the first twelve layers rather than to capacity. We plan one pilot run on a tenth of the Senna safety prompts to check that agreement with the reference labels is not saturated before the full experiment.
CONTROLS: (1) Shuffle the labels of the Senna safety prompts as a negative control for agreement with the reference labels. (2) Ablate freezing the first twelve layers alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on agreement with the reference labels. (3) Match the number of training steps between Corvane-12 and Dromond-8. (4) Repeat the evaluation of agreement with the reference labels on the Senna safety prompts with a second prompt template. (5) Run Corvane-12 on the Senna safety prompts with five random seeds and report the spread of agreement with the reference labels.
COST: 18 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Agreement with the reference labels degrades on the Marisol summaries while it holds on the Senna safety prompts.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of truncating the context to 2,000 tokens on pass rate on hidden tests for Pelleas-4
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Pelleas-4 on the Wexcombe caption set and measure pass rate on hidden tests before and after truncating the context to 2,000 tokens. The hypothesis is that truncating the context to 2,000 tokens changes pass rate on hidden tests on the Wexcombe caption set by more than run-to-run noise. A null result on pass rate on hidden tests would still be informative if exact-match accuracy on the Pryce reasoning chains also stays within its usual range. All runs share one data order for the Wexcombe caption set, so that differences in pass rate on hidden tests cannot come from batching. We compare against Marrow-3, trained with the same budget on the Wexcombe caption set. The comparison between Pelleas-4 and Marrow-3 uses the same decoding settings and the same evaluation script. We report pass rate on hidden tests separately for short and long inputs of the Wexcombe caption set, since truncating the context to 2,000 tokens may act differently on each.
CONTROLS: (1) Ablate truncating the context to 2,000 tokens alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on pass rate on hidden tests. (2) Shuffle the labels of the Wexcombe caption set as a negative control for pass rate on hidden tests. (3) Run Pelleas-4 on the Wexcombe caption set with five random seeds and report the spread of pass rate on hidden tests. (4) Report exact-match accuracy on the Wexcombe caption set to check that the gain is not an artifact of one metric. (5) Evaluate on the Pryce reasoning chains as a held-out distribution.
COST: 7 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in pass rate on hidden tests beyond seed noise on the Wexcombe caption set.

- id: c1 | description: Evaluate on the Lowick tabular benchmark, a distribution that was not used for training.
- id: c2 | description: Use the Senna safety prompts with shuffled labels as a negative control for agreement with the reference labels.
